result.killer: No full killer found. Two parts of the idea are weaker than claimed. First, according to StartupCafe's summary of a draft government decision, WorkinRomania itself refuses to generate a request once an agency exceeds the number of workers its authorisation covers. That means the platform enforces guarantee headroom. Second, the same draft has the platform automatically check contracts against the job offer, COR code and REGES-ONLINE records. Both points come from the draft and may change before adoption.
result.reason: I found no commercial product for Romanian placement contracts, guarantees or worker rosters. That held in Romanian and English searches and among law-firm alerts (KPMG, Kinstellar, Crowe). The state platform weakens the pitch, though. Per a draft government decision (StartupCafe), it blocks requests above the authorised worker count, which covers guarantee headroom. It also auto-checks contracts against the job offer and REGES. What is left is mainly filling in the bilingual Ordin 655 contracts and keeping roster and permit deadlines, which is thin. The market is small and shrinking: the importers' employers' association PIFM expects 70-80% of small agencies to exit. I found no official count of authorised agencies. Parliament has not finished amending the ordinance: Senate changes, PLx 427/2026 still in Chamber committees in September, and Profit.ro reports relaxed rules for some agencies.

result.killer: Law 88/2026 made RO e-Factura optional for hosts renting under their CNP (individuals). MEDAT said in June 2026 that issuance of EU 2024/1028 unique codes had not begun and depended on the technical solution and budget. The minister targets a legal framework by the end of 2026, so the main trigger is deferred.
result.reason: Both new triggers have fallen away for now. 1) The e-Factura duty was removed. Law 88/2026 (Monitorul Oficial, 29 May 2026, in force 1 Jun 2026) made RO e-Factura optional for individuals taxed under their CNP, which covers hosts renting in hotel regime. 2) The unique code has not started. As of 10 Jun 2026, MEDAT said no unique codes under Reg. 2024/1028 were being issued, with timing depending on the technical solution and budget. The minister expects the legal framework only by the end of 2026, and Booking will enforce only once Romania launches the registry. I found nothing newer, so the code duty is unverified and may still be months away. What remains is old and handled by accountants: the annual D212, the monthly 301/390 VAT on platform commissions, and the accommodation occupancy sheet. The market size is still unknown.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers

ITM enforcement on security firms is heavy (a 600k lei fine in Bucharest). No 2026 change for temporary-work agencies found. The reform lowers the burden, so it is weak.

It brings certification of construction firms by experience and specialisation. Site managers (diriginți de șantier) gained fire-safety duties in a March 2026 ordinance. Site managers are authorised by ISC, and the technical book of the building is their duty (fine up to 10k lei). No e-Construcții duty for small firms confirmed.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports

ONPCSB's own free portal handles reporting.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 applies from 20 May 2026. Every short-term rental unit needs a unique registration code, issued through SITUR (login by ROeID or e-signature) and shown in the listing. In May 2026 code generation was not yet available. Platforms will delist listings with no valid code and report monthly data. The MEDAT minister also announced a digital guest slip. Tax: forfait of 30% of gross for 1-7 rooms, special VAT code with Form 301 and 390 for platform commissions, and ANAF found tens of thousands of undeclared hosts in one county. RO e-Factura for individual hosts by CNP from 1 Jun 2026 (Form 082 by 26 May) is contradicted by a source saying Law 88/2026 (MO 459, 29 May 2026) made it optional. Local tourist promotion taxes: Sibiu 2% from Jan 2026, Brașov 1 leu per tourist per day (draft). The 2011-13 SIET tourist register never launched.

coverage.category: 33. Beverage retailers under the SGR deposit-return system

It must report with the administrator's own software. Garda de Mediu fines are heavy (over 760k lei in one round, up to 50k lei per refusal to refund the deposit). coverage.category: 34. Natural-gas installation inspection firms (ANRE EDIB/PDIB) and households and HOAs as consumers

Authorised firms must keep a current register of verifications and revisions per contracted consumption point. The network operator can cut supply when the verification is missing. A draft would let the 10-year revision replace that year's verification (adoption unconfirmed). Appliances are separately checked by ISCIR-authorised operators.

coverage.category: 35. Gambling halls and slot-room operators (ONJN)
coverage.found: The 2025-26 reforms (Law 141/2025 package) add ONJN binding orders. A public register of gaming devices with map and QR codes was announced for 15 Oct 2025. A March 2026 emergency ordinance reportedly requires a local operating authorisation in addition to the national licence. A self-exclusion unification draft is pending. ONJN ran about 7,000 checks in its first year, with fines near 8.1M lei. The sector is chain-dominated, so it is weak.

coverage.category: 36. Agricultural producers selling directly: producer attestation and sales booklet (Law 145/2014)
coverage.found: Individual producers need an atestat de producător (valid 1 year, visa by the mayor each half year) and a carnet de comercializare, with a sheet handed to each buyer. Mayors keep a register. This is a paper process, and fines reach 22,500 lei in older sources. No digital version found in 2026. Duty-holders are individuals and the registers belong to city halls.

coverage.category: 37. Fire safety (ISU) authorisations for businesses
coverage.found: OUG 17/2026 (in force Mar 2026) amends Law 307/2006. Authorisations can be suspended when detection, extinguishing or lighting systems do not work or documentation is missing, with about 30 days to fix. There is no warning for many firm offences, and reduced-fine payment is withdrawn for serious ones. IGSU must publish a live list of authorisations. A MAI draft would force medium firms to form fire-protection technical commissions (final form unconfirmed). No mandatory PSI register or periodic deadline for SMEs confirmed.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated product. Searches returned generic recruitment and agency software (Zoho Recruit, Voyager, Daftra), none covering Romanian placement contracts or guarantees. Agilion is a recruitment agency, not a software vendor. WorkinRomania.gov.ro, the free state platform, does registration, agency and employer authorisation, single applications and public registers. Per the Digi24 article and the Rubinian summary of Ordin 655, it does not generate the placement contracts (the agency drafts them from the model) and nothing indicates it tracks guarantee headroom. I did not check whether it has an API or export.
result.duty: Confirmed in force. OUG 32/2026 (MO 335, 27 Apr 2026) replaced OG 25/2014. Only ANOFM-authorised agencies may place foreigners, and they apply online via WorkinRomania.gov.ro, which has run since about 6-8 Aug 2026. Before authorisation an agency must post a 75,000 EUR guarantee (Treasury deposit or Romanian bank letter) for up to 250 workers, plus 50,000 EUR per extra 250. It must keep the guarantee topped up for the whole authorisation or face suspension or withdrawal. Fines run up to 40,000 lei. Employers can authorise themselves instead, with a 1,000 EUR guarantee per worker. Ordin 655/2026 sets three mandatory model contracts: service contract plus job offer, placement contract, and employment contract. They must be in Romanian plus a language the worker understands, signed before the visa, and contracts missing mandatory elements are absolutely void. The employment contract must also be registered in REGES-Online. Open caveats: on 26 May 2026 the Senate adopted amendments that relax some agency obligations, and I could not find the Chamber vote or the final guarantee figure. In September 2026 the Bucharest Court of Appeal suspended the shortage-occupation list order.
result.market: I found no official count of authorised agencies; ANOFM announced the first authorisations without giving a number. One source puts it at about 15,000 companies importing foreign labour, a figure that covers employers, not just agencies. IGI counted 148,272 non-EU workers with valid permits (Feb 2026). PIFM expects about 70% of small and mid-size agencies to exit because of the guarantee, so the number of agencies that will buy is probably in the low hundreds. Self-authorised employers are a second, larger but less pressed segment.
result.reason: The duty is real. The pool of buyers is small and shrinking: PIFM expects about 70% of small agencies to exit. The rules are still moving: the Senate amended the OUG, the Chamber vote is unverified, and a court suspended the shortage-occupation list. Contract templates alone are a thin product.

result.competitor: No dedicated Romanian host-compliance software found in 3 competitor searches, but software tools were only partly checked, so this is unverified. result.duty: Partly in force. In force: classification certificate required under HG 1267/2010, fine 40,000-50,000 lei for operating without it (MEDAT, cited by StartupCafe on 10 Jun 2026). Special VAT code (art. 317 Fiscal Code) with monthly Form 301 and Form 390 by the 25th, only in months with platform commission invoices. Annual D212. ANAF has said hosts need a cash register. Not in force: the unique registration code under EU Reg. 2024/1028 through SITUR. MEDAT said on 10 Jun 2026 that code issuance had not started and the national method was under analysis. Still described as forthcoming on 3 Aug 2026. No later order found. Law 88/2026 (Official Gazette no. 459, 29 May 2026) made RO e-Factura optional for individuals with only a CNP, so the 1 Jun 2026 e-Factura obligation is refuted.
result.market: About 74,000 apartments and rooms offered for short-term rental in Romania (European Travel Commission data via ZF, cited by StartupCafe on 3 Aug 2026), up 7.8% year on year. Number of hosts not found.
result.reason: The headline trigger is not live yet. On 10 Jun 2026 the tourism ministry (MEDAT) said Romania had not started issuing unique codes under EU Regulation 2024/1028 and was still deciding how to implement it. As of 3 Aug 2026 the code was still described as a future duty, and I found no order or national law since. Law 88/2026 made e-Factura optional for hosts with only a CNP (no company), so that part of the claim is refuted. The duties that are in force are the monthly 301/390 VAT returns on platform commissions (via the special VAT code), the annual D212, the classification certificate under HG 1267/2010 (fines of 40,000 to 50,000 lei) and a cash register. About 74,000 units are listed. I found no dedicated product, only accountants. This search only partly checked software tools, so competition is unverified. The score could go up if SITUR starts issuing codes.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated SaaS for EDIB firms to manage clients, expiry dates and fișe after 3 Romanian-language searches. Flam Install (iOS, Innovative Sharks Dsoft SRL) is a free app for one firm's customers, with booking and payment history. Distributors keep the official database of verifications and revisions and send due-date notices. Distrigaz Sud Rețele runs an online portal for authorised firms, at least for commissioning requests. Large suppliers and distributors sell bundled verification services (Engie ASIGAZ), which competes for the end customer. Generic field-service or ERP tools: not checked.
result.duty: ANRE Order 179/2015 procedure (in force since 1 Jan 2016; amended by Orders 71/2020 and 96/2023; December 2025 consolidation published by Gazest). The final customer must have a periodic verification at most every 2 years and a revision at most every 10 years, plus after more than 6 months out of use or an incident. Only ANRE-authorised firms do this work (EDIB, or ET depending on pressure), recording it on a regulated fișă de evidență. The distributor or supplier can cut supply until proof is shown. Distributors must keep a database of the fișe that the authorised firms register. The Competition Council fined Delgaz Grid about 30m lei, partly for registering fișe late. The draft letting a revision replace that year's verification (profit.ro) is still unconfirmed as adopted. The Gazest PDF could not be parsed, so I took the article-level detail from secondary sources.
result.market: About 4 million gas consumption points (household and non-household; economedia, 2025), so roughly 2 million verifications a year. I did not find the number of EDIB-authorised firms: the ANRE public register exists but was not reached. Since each firm needs at least 3 authorised installers, it is plausibly several hundred to a few thousand firms (an estimate, not verified).
result.reason: The duty is real. Under ANRE Order 179/2015 (amended by Orders 71/2020 and 96/2023), gas user installations need a verification at least every 2 years and a revision at least every 10 years, done only by EDIB-authorised firms. Each job produces a regulated fișă de evidență, and supply can be cut until proof is shown. I found no firm-side SaaS, only Flam Install, a customer booking app from one firm. Three things limit the opportunity. The distributors (Delgaz, DSR) by rule keep the database of these checks, and distributors and suppliers already remind customers. Big suppliers sell packaged inspection services (Engie ASIGAZ). The EDIB firms are small trades businesses that are hard to reach and pay little. I did not find the EDIB firm count. I could not confirm that the draft letting a revision replace that year's verification has been adopted.

OUG 53/2025 (Government sitting of 2 Oct 2025, replacing OG 4/1995) is confirmed only through secondary sources. I could not read the final text (the ANF PDF was unreadable). The old regime (OG 41/2007) required a registration certificate with an annual visa for sellers. Whether the final act mandates a sales register, police/ITM registration, or sets fines for distributors is unconfirmed. The 35,000 lei figure comes from press coverage aimed at farmers. No Romanian PPP-shop software turned up. The only comparable product is Italian (Passepartout Mexal), which prints the load/unload register and annual SIAN export. The number of shops was not found. The market is small and fragmented, and ERP vendors may already cover the register. Score stays at 3.

The duty is real. From 1 July 2026, N1 vans of 2.5-3.5 t in international carriage and cabotage need a G2V2 smart tachograph, with driver and company cards. Driver cards are downloaded every 28 days and the vehicle unit every 90 days. I did not confirm a Romanian fine schedule; a Suceava tachograph shop claims 4,000-6,000 lei, which is commercial and unsourced. The archive period is unconfirmed; a Moldovan source says at least 1 year. Competition is strong. SVT Electronics (Romanian, TachoSafe RDU and Web), Frotcom and MAN RIO Compliant already do remote download and archiving. I found no count of affected vans. Buyers are micro-firms with low willingness to pay, and many already use fleet vendors. Weak niche.

Duty is real: OUG 190/2000 requires ANPC authorisation, 10-day change notices and 7-day notice for temporary activity. ANPC checked 80+ traders on 29 Jan 2026 and issued 148 fines (260k+ lei). I found no Romanian software for this register. Generic jewellery ERPs exist (GoldMatrix is India-focused). I could not confirm the number of authorised operators, the register format, or the date of the state-mark and doubled-fines rule. The profit.ro page returned 403. Playtech (2022) mentions doubled fines and a hologram mark, so that change may be old. Weak case: a small niche, mostly one-off notices, the register is probably covered by stock tools, and the doubled-fines claim is unverified. A recurring SaaS looks hard to sell.

The duty is real. CARs are non-profit associations that keep accounts under OMFP 1969/2007 and file annual balance sheets. A specialist (Nov 2024) says they also file D406 SAF-T, monthly or quarterly, because they fall under the non-profit category in OPANAF 1783/2021. That is an opinion, not an ANAF ruling, and no penalty was cited. Competition is only partly checked. Member-facing CAR apps exist (UNCAR, ASCAR, Membri C.A.R.), which implies back-office software exists, but I did not identify it. Market data is old: about 1,659 employee CARs (2015) and about 135 pensioner CARs (2017). Buyers are scattered, volunteer-run and low-budget, and many use an external accountant. Pain is moderate but willingness to pay is weak.

Duty is real: Law 292/2011 requires provider accreditation plus service licensing. The tougher amendment was promulgated 16 Apr 2024 (stiripesurse): 3-month provisional licence, inspection within 15 days, fines up to 100k lei, first criminal sanctions, free licensing, and a unified electronic register run by the ministry. The Cluj 80k lei fine is also real. I found no dedicated Romanian compliance software, but I ran only two searches and the competitor check is thin. The duty is mainly one-off or episodic (licence, then renewal and inspections), not a regular filing calendar. The market is small (about 1,700 operators), and unlicensed homes won't buy. Pain is high, but frequency, buyer count and willingness to pay are weak, so the opportunity is niche. Entry-into-force dates and the final law number were not verified.

result.reason: The duty is real. Law 105/2023 requires monthly stock data by the 15th for the previous month, via the MADR/AFIR portal SERSPAR. Fines run from 5,000 to 20,000 lei. Exempt: shops up to 400 sqm, street traders and caterers. No 2026 change found. Not checked: current thresholds, real enforcement, bulk upload, and the number of small operators covered (no register figure found). No third-party competitor search was run. The free state portal does the core filing. Any product would only be a done-for-you filing service or an ERP export, which is a thin niche. Buyers are fragmented and the duty looks like a form that is quick to fill in. Score 3.

CATUC (Legea 169/2026) was published 10 Aug and in force 25 Aug 2026, with a new certification of construction firms by experience and specialisation, per search summaries of profit.ro. But criteria, body, deadline, penalty and whether micro-contractors are covered could not be found. The profit.ro page returned 403 on fetch. ARACO/AIIR say the mechanism is unclear. Certification seems tied to public procurement, so it is likely not a recurring duty for small contractors. Competition: only generic construction CRM/site-diary tools were found (Zarina CRM, Site Productivity, Daily Report App); none targets the diriginte de șantier legal duties. Market size was not checked. The idea is weak and premature until the implementing norms appear.

Duty is partly real: Law 196/2018 sets simple-entry bookkeeping for associations, with fines of 4,000-9,000 lei for using the repair fund for current expenses. I found no authoritative source for the claimed D100 semester / D205 duties. Forums conflict on D100, D205 and civil-contract admins, and D112 only applies if someone is paid. Competition: HomeFile (about 3,000 associations, 2022 article) and E-Bloc cover collections and payment lists. I could not confirm whether they generate D112/D205. Association count (about 100,000) not verified. Most associations have no paid payroll, so the fiscal-filing niche is thin. The 2026 Law 196 amendments and the SAF-T exemption for associations were not confirmed. Buyers are volunteers with low willingness to pay.

The duty is real but sits with suppliers, not prosumers. Law 160/2026 (in force 26 Jul 2026) makes the supplier calculate and invoice monthly. The Tax Code change raises the exemption from issuing invoices for grid deliveries from 27 kW to 900 kW, so the buyer group is relieved of paperwork. The 900 kW figure is only the invoice-exemption and imbalance threshold. Compensation covers installations up to 400 kW, with day-ahead financial regularisation at 200-400 kW. The ANRE draft of 20 Aug is still in consultation. I found no prosumer filing duty and no software competitor, but the need is weak. Market size was not found. The sources do not say who issues the invoices under the new rules.
